description: OPTIONAL harder tier for llm-benchmark, meant for model-vs-model comparison, NOT day-to-day regression runs. Run explicitly with: python3 benchmark.py run --questions hard_questions.json ... These questions target things a strong model can still get wrong on the merits (subtle language semantics, undefined behavior, exploit/RE reasoning). Every predict-the-output question was executed or compiled (CPython 3.11, gcc/g++ 13) to obtain its ground-truth answer.

questions.prompt:
What does this Python program print?
def f(x, acc=[]):
    acc.append(x)
    return acc
f(1)
f(2)
print(f(3))
Respond with only the exact output, nothing else.

This is an x86-64 function (System V AMD64 ABI: the first integer argument arrives in edi/rdi, the return value goes in eax/rax):

mov eax, edi
imul eax, eax
add eax, edi
ret

What value does it return when called with the argument 6? Respond with only the decimal number.

This is an x86-64 function (System V AMD64 ABI: first integer argument in rdi, return value in rax):

lea rax, [rdi + rdi*4]
ret

What value does it return when called with the argument 6? Respond with only the decimal number.
The four bytes at increasing memory addresses are: 0x78 0x56 0x34 0x12. Interpreted as a little-endian unsigned 32-bit integer, what is their value in decimal? Respond with only the number.

On x86-64, a function's stack frame lays out, from lower to higher addresses: a local buffer char buf[32], then the 8-byte saved RBP, then the 8-byte saved return address. Starting from the first byte of buf, how many bytes must a linear overflow write before it begins overwriting the saved return address? Respond with only the number.
A string was obfuscated by XORing each byte with the key 0x20. One resulting byte is 0x48. What is the original ASCII character (before obfuscation)? Respond with only the single character.
